title: Boxed vs Unboxed Memory Explorer
description: Side-by-side boxed and unboxed memory diagrams for the same float addition, stepped in lockstep with a running memory-operation tally.
creator: Real-Time DSP on a $5 Microcontroller
author: Dan McCreary
subject: Digital Signal Processing
Memory Layout
Optimization

learningObjectives: Explain why boxed arithmetic needs more memory accesses
Compare boxed and unboxed memory layouts step by step
Explain why the result allocation matters most for real-time code

controls.label: Show operation tally
controls.purpose: Show or hide the running counts

assumptions: Operation counts are illustrative, not a precise cycle count
Both operands are floats already resident in memory
limitations: Does not model interpreter dispatch overhead, which adds further cost to the boxed path beyond the memory operations shown

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Lockstep step-through of two representations with a running tally
keyQuestions: Which step allocates, and why does that matter most?
What safety property does unboxing remove?
commonMisconceptions: That a float variable holds a float
That the cost difference is only about speed rather than also about predictability
assessmentOpportunities: Estimate allocations per butterfly and their cumulative consequence
